one_liner: Senior ICE headquarters specialist supporting crime victims through the VOICE program with crisis intervention, referrals and partner outreach, plus briefing leadership.
fit_summary: Daniel's people skills, relationship-building and government-client consulting at IEM fit the partnership and outreach duties. GS-13 requires a year of GS-12-equivalent experience in 3 of 4 victim-services areas, such as compensation applications, crisis intervention and victim-organization outreach, and nothing on file shows direct victim work. Unless Daniel's IEM role involved disaster survivor case work or crisis support, qualifying will be hard.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens) under Direct Hire Authority; no federal status or veterans' preference needed.

Basic requirement: a behavioral or social science degree (transcripts required), equivalent education plus experience, or four years of experience showing that knowledge. Check whether a political science or public policy degree counts as a related social science.

Specialized experience: one year at GS-12 equivalent doing 3 or more of the following: victim compensation applications, crisis intervention and referrals, outreach to victim assistance organizations, and working relationships with federal, state or local officials.
Must be able to obtain a Secret clearance.
All qualifications must be met by the closing date, October 30, 2026.
strategy: Before applying, confirm honestly whether your IEM work included direct contact with disaster survivors, such as intake, assistance applications, crisis support or referrals. That is your only realistic route to 3 of the 4 specialized items.

Frame IEM duties in the posting's terms but in your own words, since the posting rejects copy-pasted language. Survivor assistance programs map to compensation applications, and coordination with FEMA, state and local emergency managers maps to cooperative working relationships with officials.
Count volunteer work such as crisis hotlines, victim advocacy or community service; the posting credits it. List hours per week for each role.
Upload transcripts even if you qualify by experience, and note relevant behavioral or social science coursework.
Answer the questionnaire accurately, because overstating can remove you. Prepare for the online competency assessment, and submit well before October 30.
If you don't qualify at GS-13, target GS-9/11 victim-services, FEMA or emergency management roles, or Virginia and local victim-witness programs to build qualifying experience.
resume_bullets: [Title], IEM, [dates], [hours]/week: Coordinated with [federal/state/local agency] officials on [disaster recovery program], building partnerships that [describe outcome].
Assisted [number] [disaster survivors/residents] with [assistance/benefit applications] and referred them to [services], [frequency].
Prepared [briefings/reports] for [client leadership] on [program operations], resulting in [process change, if any].
interview_questions: Describe a time you supported someone in crisis. What did you do, and what referrals did you make?
How have you built a working relationship with officials at another agency to reach a shared goal?
How do you manage stress and stay professional in emotionally difficult conversations?
How would you prepare a briefing for leadership on improving a victim program's operations?
watch_outs: The specialized experience is victim-services specific, and Daniel's background may not meet GS-13 equivalency.
The application window is short: October 19–30, 2026.
A Secret clearance is required, and there is no promotion potential beyond GS-13.
VOICE is a politically sensitive program, so be ready to discuss the mission neutrally.
